Public engagement with the project increased after the survey.
committed: pledged or dedicated resources or effort to something
đã cam kết, đã bỏ ra
She has committed years of her life to environmental research.
suffer: to experience something unpleasant, such as pain or loss
Farmers suffer most when the rains fail two years running.
budget: a plan for how money will be spent
The family set a tight budget for their summer vacation.
cuts: removes or shortens part of something, often abruptly
The new alarm cuts short a large part of the night's dreaming sleep.
think: to use the mind to consider something or form an opinion
I need some time to think before I answer you.
should: used to say what is correct, expected, or advisable
You should see a doctor if the pain continues for another week.
main: The main entrance to the museum faces the river.
best: of the highest quality or most excellent
This bakery makes the best bread in the whole neighbourhood.
salmon: a large edible fish with pink flesh, or its pinkish colour
They grilled fresh salmon with lemon and herbs for dinner.
fillet: a piece of boneless meat or fish
She grilled a salmon fillet for dinner.
anywhere: in, at, or to any place
With this app you can book a hotel room almost anywhere in the world.
would: used to express a hypothetical or past future action
Fifty years ago, people asked which jobs machines would take first.
see: to perceive something with the eyes
From the hilltop you can see the whole valley below.
directors: people who manage or oversee an organization
The board of directors will meet next week to review the budget.
understand: to grasp the meaning or nature of something
The question sounds simple: do people understand less when they read on a screen?
establishment: a business, organisation, or the act of setting one up
The cultural experience of an establishment matters as much as its food.
important: It is important to drink enough water during exercise.
sustained: continuing steadily over a long period without stopping
The choir held a long, sustained note at the end of the hymn.
viability: the ability to work successfully or survive
khả năng tồn tại, tính khả thi
Investors questioned the long-term viability of the business plan.
rooted: firmly established, often based on a particular origin
bắt nguồn từ, gắn liền với
Her cooking style is deeply rooted in family tradition.
gap: a difference or space between two things
The gap between rich and poor neighbourhoods keeps growing.
those: used to refer to people or things further away or already mentioned
Those houses on the hill were built a century ago.
foundations: the basic structures or principles on which something is built
Early education lays the foundations for lifelong learning.
becomes: The sky becomes darker earlier as autumn approaches.
harder: more difficult or more solid; comparative of hard
The second exam was noticeably harder than the first.
ignore: pay no attention to something deliberately
It is hard to ignore such an obvious warning sign.
consistent: always behaving or happening in the same way
The runner kept a consistent pace throughout the entire race.
frameworks: basic structures of ideas or rules that support systems
Different countries use different legal frameworks to regulate banks.
particularly: especially, more than usual or more than others
The traffic gets particularly bad on Friday evenings near the bridge.
standardization: the process of making things follow the same standard
Standardization of parts made repairs much cheaper.
could: past tense of can, used to express ability or possibility
She could speak three languages fluently by the age of ten.
give: to hand over or provide something to someone
Please give the documents to the manager before noon.
currently: The company is currently hiring for several new positions.
lacks: does not have something that is needed (he/she/it)
The plan lacks a clear timeline for completion.
